name: Liquid Glass
visualIdentity: Explicit optical glass treatment: clear boundaries, plausible refraction, edge highlights, limited dispersion, and a recognizable background seen through the form. Droplets, lenses, or flexible panels may deform while refraction follows continuously. Ordinary translucent blur is not liquid glass.
suitableUses: Strong for hero optical moments, abstract brand loops, fluid UI concepts, and product or feature launches centered on clarity. The supplied text also lists editorial and product narratives as compatible, though these are broader suitability notes rather than defining style traits. Works in video and interactive HTML.
limitations: Keep text outside refracting areas and preserve legibility and stable boundaries. Avoid excessive dispersion or overlapping lenses; do not claim simulated fluid motion is physically accurate without validated simulation. Screen-space displacement is an explicitly labeled 2D approximation. Use motion patterns only when their scene elements and narrative fit; omit stacking that hides needed copy, chapter transitions that break a continuous shot, or orbit without real 3D depth or labeled parallax.
palette: No intrinsic palette is specified. The example tokens for new presentation elements only are background #EDEBE3, foreground #293C49, accent #91ACB0; they are optional and subordinate to task colors, brand/reference colors, existing semantic roles, and source asset colors. Keep discrete tokens; gradients are disabled. Preserve approved values and color families, and check text on actual composited glass and imagery; the listed contrast ratios cover opaque pairs only.
motionAndInteraction: Use coherent deformation and keep refraction tied to the same changing surface. Video state must derive from shared, seekable composition time, with deterministic replay or cached simulation and no dependence on live input. Interactive HTML may use bounded pointer tilt, scroll progress, swipe/snap, or camera orbit only when the selected pattern fits; provide readable states, reverse behavior, and appropriate keyboard, touch, and reduced-motion alternatives. One owner per animated property.
audio: No fixed soundtrack is specified. Choose music, narration, vocals, effects, ambience, or silence for the topic and explicit audio requirements; do not infer playback or spatial sound from visual depth. Use verified audio assets or analysis, synchronize through the composition timeline, and check intelligibility, balance, clipping, and picture sync.
assetRequirements: Use Three.js for 3D geometry and rendering, MeshPhysicalMaterial transmission/IOR/roughness for glass, and offscreen-rendered background textures for material sampling; avoid active-target feedback. Native Canvas or SVG is possible without a 3D engine. Preserve recognizable background content, source imagery, exact copy, and readable typography. Prepare or cache stateful simulations; distinguish simulated appearance from photographed production. HyperFrames is the primary video assembly/export pipeline; Remotion is allowed only if unavailable or a verified required capability is blocked, with reason recorded.
combinations: Liquid Glass alone suits hero optical moments. With style-114, droplet merge/split choreography can drive deformation while refraction follows the same surface; minimal dispersion, no refracting text, and a recognizable background are constraints. With style-096, restrained product pacing and typography frame one lens or panel; keep titles outside it and avoid overlapping lenses or rainbow-heavy dispersion. Other supplied patterns—card stacking, voice-card tilt, chapter handoffs, carousel, orb deformation, storytelling, and camera orbit—are optional examples, not automatic combinations; select only with scene-specific justification.
productionApproach: Choose renderer and motion method for visual fidelity first: Three.js/materials and offscreen background sampling for 3D, or labeled screen-space displacement for 2D. Keep rendering, motion, and composition/export responsibilities distinct. HyperFrames owns assembly, seekable timing, media/audio sync, validation, and export; use paused GSAP timelines as needed. Remotion is a documented conditional fallback, not a visual renderer. For interactive HTML, bind suitable patterns to actual scroll/pointer/input and provide accessible alternatives. Inspect representative states and decoded output for refraction continuity, boundaries, text, assets, timing, and audio.
